title: Phase-Sensitive Heterodyne Detection of MW using EIT Harmonics in Rydberg Atoms
authors: Mangesh Bhattarai, Rishav Hui, Sumanta Khan, Vineet Bharti, Vasant Natarajan, Kanhaiya Pandey
abstract: We investigate the generation and characterization of higher-order harmonics in the probe-laser absorption arising from nonlinear interactions in an electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) ladder system involving Rydberg states and driven by two microwave fields in the heterodyne configuration. We characterize the amplitude and phase of the generated harmonics as a function of the relative frequency and phase of the applied microwave fields. The phase of the $n^{\mathrm{th}}$ harmonic follows the relation $φ_n=nφ$, demonstrating phase multiplication and suggesting that higher-order harmonics may offer an enhanced phase response for phase-sensitive measurements. We further characterize the harmonic amplitudes and bandwidths and find that the measured bandwidths are significantly larger than the intrinsic Rydberg-state linewidth, consistent with power broadening under the experimental conditions. The experimental observations are supported by density-matrix calculations, which reproduce the key features of the measured harmonic response.
summary: This research demonstrates a method for phase-sensitive microwave detection using Rydberg atoms in an EIT ladder system. By analyzing the higher-order harmonics generated in the probe absorption, the authors show that the phase of these harmonics scales linearly with the harmonic order. This technique offers an enhanced phase response compared to conventional electrometry.
main_problem: The paper investigates generating and characterizing higher-order harmonics in the probe-laser absorption arising from nonlinear interactions within an Electromagnetically Induced Transparency (EIT) ladder system driven by two microwave fields.
main_result: The detection method demonstrates phase multiplication, where the phase of the $n$-th harmonic follows $\phi_n = n\phi$, suggesting an enhanced phase response for phase-sensitive microwave measurements.
method: The study combines theoretical density-matrix calculations (using Floquet expansion) with experimental measurements of probe absorption as a function of microwave field detuning and phase.
model_or_system: The physical system utilizes Rydberg atoms in a ladder-type EIT configuration, driven by a probe laser, a control laser, and two microwave fields in a heterodyne setup. The dynamics are modeled using the Lindblad master equation.
key_observables: Amplitude and phase of generated harmonics ($n=1, 2, 3, ...$), probe absorption rate, and the splitting of the EIT resonance ($\Omega_{MW}$).
important_parameters: Relative frequency and phase of the applied microwave fields, and the ratio of measured bandwidths to the intrinsic Rydberg-state linewidth (showing power broadening).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the density matrix formalism and the Floquet expansion to treat the time-periodic driving fields.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the energy level diagram, the transition from sinusoidal to pulsed absorption as MW fields increase, and plots showing the harmonic absorption response versus beat frequency or detuning.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the nonlinear interaction mechanism in the EIT system, then details the theoretical framework using density matrices and Floquet analysis, and finally presents experimental measurements confirming harmonic generation and phase dependence.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, non-linear quantum optical technique to measure microwave phase shifts with enhanced sensitivity by leveraging high-order harmonic generation in Rydberg atoms, which is a key area in quantum sensing.
